title: add-vpc-control-plane-provisioning-multi-az-peering-endpoints-sgs-route53-dns
author: Anjali Rao
body: Motivation: add end-to-end Terraform and installer changes to provision the Private Control Plane VPC for private deployments across multiple AZs. This PR centralizes subnet creation, interface/endpoints (S3, ECR, KMS, EC2), security group templates, cross-account VPC peering, and Route53 private hosted zone configuration so that the private installer can bring up a fully routable control plane for on-prem/VPC customers. Summary of changes: 1) New Terraform module modules/vpc-control-plane that creates multi-AZ internal subnets (private and management), NAT gateways for outbound control-plane egress, interface endpoints for core AWS services (S3, ECR, STS, KMS), and VPC endpoints for Kinesis/CloudWatch if enabled via flags. 2) Security group templates and least-privileged SG rules for control-plane tiers (control-plane API, management plane, worker-to-controlplane), exported as module outputs to be consumed by customer VPC peering and on-prem connectors. 3) Automated Route53 private hosted zone and resolver rules with cross-account delegation option and explicit records for control-plane endpoints. 4) VPC peering and route propagation helpers with optional AWS Transit Gateway flag; peering resource supports cross-account accept via a separate cross-account-accept module. 5) Updates to the private-installer chart and bootstrap scripts to consume the new module outputs and to document an automated upgrade/rollback flow: terraform plan -> apply -> helm upgrade --install, with a safe canary for DNS changes. 6) Helm chart adjustments: added values for interfaceEndpoints.enabled, route53.delegated_domain, and securityGroups.controlPlaneId to wire Terraform outputs to chart values. 7) Tests: smoke TF integration plan in perf-canary, unit tests for terraform module with Terratest examples, and local end-to-end smoke script under redwood-private-installer/test/integration. Upgrade notes and migration: this PR includes a migration script terraform/migrate/v1_to_v2.sh that safely renames older state resources used by earlier single-AZ control plane modules; the script is non-destructive by default and logs required manual steps when cross-account peering exists. Rollback: terraform plan and state snapshot steps added to private-installer pre-hook; Helm hooks will revert Route53 records in case of failed install. Backwards compatibility: module exposes optional inputs to mimic legacy resource names (legacy_subnet_ids, legacy_sg_ids) so existing customers can opt-in to the new module without immediate rework. Security considerations: created least-privileged SGs, explicit KMS key alias usage and endpoints for private ECR/S3 access; audit logging enabled via module flag and documented on README. Testing & rollout: validated in staging account with multi-AZ setup (us-west-2a/b/c) using the perf-canary suite and internal cluster smoke tests; Route53 delegation tested with a cross-account delegate in a partner account. See linked Linear ENG-4721 for rollout plan. Related: updates several quickstarts and docs pages to include new Terraform variables and example usage.

review_comments:
Lucas Chen: Please split the large main.tf into smaller logical files (subnets, endpoints, sg) to make future diffs readable. Also add tagging for all resources compliant with billing tagging policy.
Author (Anjali Rao): Split into subnet.tf, endpoints.tf, security_groups.tf and added tags module usage. Updated commit b2c3d4e -> b2c3d4e2.
Priya Natarajan: Need to add explicit tests for DNS propagation failure and a retry strategy for the Route53 delegation step; otherwise DNS rollover can leave services unreachable.
Author: Added a retry helper in preapply.sh and a test scenario in perf-canary to simulate delayed delegation.
Omar Haddad: LGTM for networking rules but please confirm that the cross-account peering flow is optional and does not force a peering accept step on customers without cross-account setups.
Author: Confirmed peering is opt-in via variable enable_vpc_peering (default false). Documented in README.
Lucas Chen: CI showed an intermittent plan failure related to IAM role size; reduced inline policy sizes and switched several policies to managed policy attachments.
Author: Addressed; re-ran CI.
Priya Natarajan: Approved after a final run of the integration smoke tests.
Omar Haddad: Approved.
Merge: squash and merge after smoke tests passed.

merge_details: Merged by Lucas Chen using squash merge on 2025-11-20. Merge commit message: 'feat(vpc-control-plane): multi-az VPC module + installer integration, Route53 delegation, peering (ENG-4721)'. Release: targeted for private-installer v0.12.3; post-merge actions: upload terraform module to registry, cut release tag terraform/vpc-control-plane/v1.0.0, notify infra-sre channel and schedule gradual rollout in next maintenance window.
release_notes: Added a new terraform module 'vpc-control-plane' to provision multi-AZ subnets, endpoints and security groups for private control planes.
Route53 private hosted zone delegation and cross-account peering helpers added; optional via variables.
Private-installer Helm chart now accepts terraform outputs for interface endpoints and securityGroup IDs.
Migration script provided for v1 -> v2 state changes; non-destructive by default.
New integration tests and smoke scripts for multi-AZ control plane validation.
